channel.title: POLITICO Pulse
channel.description: Delivered daily by 10 a.m., Pulse examines the latest news in health care politics and policy, with special editions from the 2026 Milken Institute Future of Health Summit, Nov. 10–13.

item.title: Trump admin bets on experimental Ebola vax
item.description: The Trump administration is funding the development of an experimental vaccine in an attempt to protect against the Bundibugyo virus.
item.dc:creator: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: Trump admin rolls back health AI regulation
item.description: The Trump administration is pulling back Biden administration-era regulations that required transparency for health artificial intelligence tools.
item.dc:creator: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: RFK Jr. stumps in Michigan
item.description: This week, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. continues his midterm politicking, hoping to boost vulnerable Republican candidates ahead of next week’s elections.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: ‘Warp-speeding’ psychedelic drug access
item.description: As many as 2.1 million veterans with mental illnesses like PTSD or depression could benefit from taking psychedelic drugs like magic mushrooms or MDMA, according to a Trump official.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: RFK Jr.'s top adviser quits, MAHA reels
item.description: Members of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Healthy Again movement see the departure of his influential adviser Calley Means as a major blow to MAHA, coming just weeks before the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: By Carmen Paun, Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Carmen Paun, Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: K Street’s health care windfall
item.description: Both Republicans and Democrats look to target pharmaceutical and insurance giants’ business practices after the midterm elections. The scrutiny has the companies pouring record amounts into federal lobbying.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: Oz freezes more Medicaid funding
item.description: The Trump administration is, for the third time this year, withholding Medicaid funding from California over fraud allegations.
item.dc:creator: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: Judgment day for measles elimination nears
item.description: The U.S. is expected to learn whether the country can still claim to have “eliminated” measles next month.
item.dc:creator: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper
item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: RFK Jr. seeks food policy win
item.description: Weeks ahead of the midterm elections, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is renewing his push to address a longtime priority of his MAHA movement.

item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: Russell Brand finds support among the RFK Jr. MAHA camp

item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: Inside the FDA’s abortion pill review
item.description: The Trump administration is using software developed by a controversial vaccine researcher to conduct its safety review of the abortion pill mifepristone.

item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: A lame-duck No Surprises fix?
item.description: Rep. Greg Murphy says a plan to fix the No Surprises Act is coming soon.

item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: Minnesota’s frozen Medicaid funds
item.description: Minnesota’s top Medicaid official worries that the state could lose hundreds of millions of dollars in claims it has already paid out.

item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: Doctors decry No Surprises Act fix
item.description: Doctors are criticizing Rep. Frank Pallone’s proposal to overhaul a surprise medical billing law that providers and insurers say is riddled with problems.

item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: FDA says abortion pill review has months left
item.description: The FDA, in a Wednesday legal filing, said that its much-anticipated review of the abortion drug mifepristone won’t be completed until March.

item.dc:contributor: By Sophie Gardner and Kelly Hooper

item.title: FDA faces court test on abortion pill review
item.description: The FDA faces a court-ordered deadline today to update a federal judge in Louisiana on the status of its ongoing review of the abortion drug mifepristone, potentially shedding light on a secretive process.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: CDC’s foreign offices begin to shutter
item.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has started closing its offices abroad as President Donald Trump’s “America First” approach to foreign policy takes hold.
item.dc:creator: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner
item.dc:contributor: By Kelly Hooper and Sophie Gardner

item.title: MAHA faces new internal clash
item.description: The future of the world is being dictated in real time by the intersection of tech titans and governments. But there's just way too much tech news to monitor.

item.title: Trump’s $500 checks are in the mail

item.description: Mehmet Oz is touting lower Medicare Advantage premiums for 2027. But premiums are only part of the cost picture for the millions of people on the private plans.

item.title: MAHA’s AI bet
item.description: MAHA leaders are embracing AI to help their mission to address chronic disease, even as public unease about AI grows nationwide.

item.title: Covid vaccine rollout lags for uninsured kids

item.title: Employers seek surprise billing fix
item.description: Some of the largest U.S. companies are ramping up their lobbying efforts to reform the 2020 No Surprises Act, which protects patients from unexpected medical charges but costs millions more than anticipated.
